task_status_unchanged: PENDING (this is one validated estimator slice, not L2 acceptance)
blinding_note: The real Quaia catalogue rows were NOT read; only the catalogue row count (FITS header NAXIS2 = 755850) was used. No observed dipole was computed.

inputs.provenance_state: bundle README records upstream byte sizes and MD5 (not SHA256); SHA256 of these files NOT recomputed in this pass => SOURCE_BOUND_PARTIAL
inputs.frame_finding: random-density map vs T correlation: celestial 0.989, galactic -0.093 => selection function is in the celestial (ICRS equatorial) pixelisation

operator.command: python3 L2_quaia_estimator_pilot.py --dir <Quaia bundle dir> --gal G20.0 --nmock 120 --out L2_PILOT_RESULT_N120.json
operator.mock_model: N0=755850 points drawn from the randoms; dipole injected by thinning with acceptance (1+D.n)/(1+|D|)
operator.estimator: nside 64 pixel counts; Poisson-weighted least squares on E_p (m + d.n_p); D_hat=d/m; pixels with E<5% of mean non-zero E dropped (~42,400 pixels kept)

interpretation: Across 18 bias components (2 estimators x 3 cases x 3 axes) the largest is 2.3 standard errors; about one such value is expected by chance. No significant bias in recovering injected dipoles of 0.005 and ~0.02 is seen at this precision.
The standard error of a mean bias is sd/sqrt(n) = 1.7e-4 (null, n=120) to ~3.7e-4 (injections, n=40); biases below ~4e-4 are not excluded.
Mask/selection inflates the per-axis scatter by at most ~1.3x over the full-sky Poisson value; the estimator is close to Poisson-limited.
Using the official selection function T versus the randoms' own density as the expectation gives no significant difference in bias, despite the 0.989 correlation between them.

Mocks are drawn from the randoms themselves, so this cannot detect any difference between the real catalogue's density and the randoms/selection function (systematics, magnitude/colour/redshift-dependent selection, dust, stellar contamination).

claims.claim: The pixel Poisson-WLS dipole estimator on the Quaia G20.0 footprint recovers injected dipoles without significant bias and with near-Poisson scatter (mock-from-randoms test).
claims.limit: mocks from randoms; one tracer cut; nside 64; bias resolution ~2e-4..4e-4

claims.claim: Quaia selection function T is in celestial pixelisation.
claims.limit: frame inferred by correlation with the random density; no documentation read
